not_evidence: HAND-WRITTEN. Every harvested example is a READ response and therefore carries server-set fields (owner, created_at, url, and on a task watchers/muted/subtasks/task_actions). This example exists because a create/update body is a DIFFERENT shape from a read: build it from scratch, never echo a GET back. It is not proof the platform accepts it — tools/push-example.mjs is.
teaches: create_space: id must be ^\w+$ and is UPPERCASED server-side, so reference the space (and its task ids) by the uppercase form
statuses[] carry the board's presentation fields (color, order, complete, is_visible) and a `role` — automation moves tasks by role, never by literal id
each role is unique in the space, and a terminal role (done, lost) sits on a complete status
priorities[] need icon + icon_type + icon_color together — priorityIconClass() reads icon_type unconditionally
base_record names the record config contacts are keyed on; create_login_on_create stays false unless you mean to hand every contact a portal sign-in
create_task: the id is SERVER-GENERATED as {SPACEID}-{n}; status/priority are ids from THAT space
time is logged with add_time_log, one entry per call — the server mints the id, stamps the user and timestamps, and hydrates spent/remaining/progress onto the task
a task action write recomputes the task status by role: none done -> todo, some -> working, all -> done
a sub-task is a task with `parent`; one level deep
create_contact and create_task `identity` land the same person on one folder

identity_task.title: Follow up with the new contact

reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.was_wrong: An earlier version of this example used { "eyes": true } — a shortcode NAME. It shipped to staging, where the comment showed a broken reaction until it was corrected.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.why: The reaction key is stored VERBATIM and rendered as-is. Nothing on the platform converts a shortcode name into a glyph.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.verified_live: 2026-07-30 on comment c_EjFPH9ZyI5. Posting { "eyes": true } stored the literal string; posting { "👀": true } stored and rendered the emoji.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.fix: Pass the emoji character itself. validate_payload ERRORS on a non-emoji key.

time_logs_are_a_subresource.what: PUT /workspaces/task/{id}/time-log, one entry per call (#1292). The server mints `tl_<random>`, stamps the user from the JWT and sets created_at/updated_at. The task stores only time_tracking.estimate; logs, spent, remaining and progress_percent are hydrated on every read.
time_logs_are_a_subresource.replaced: The old contract — a client-minted logs[] array sent through update_task and replaced wholesale — is gone. Logs written that way are still in some stored tasks but nothing reads them.

task_action_moves_status_by_role.what: After a task-action write the task status is recomputed: none done -> the todo role (Awaiting Info here), some -> working (In Review), all -> done (Approved). An id the space lacks is never written.
task_action_moves_status_by_role.replaced: The 2026-08-04 finding that a write reset the task to `backlog`.

how_to_verify_on_staging: node tools/push-example.mjs --cleanup (targets QUIVA_API_URL from .env; refuses anything but staging)
or by hand: validate_payload, create_space, create_task, add_time_log twice, set_task_action, create_comment, react_to_comment
the five columns render in order with their colours; Approved and Rejected are completed columns
clean up with delete_task (delete_subtasks: true) then delete_space — both return { message: 'success' }, not 204
